items.title: Australian politics live: Labor to ‘save more than we spend’ in budget update, Chalmers says; rental affordability plummets to 14-year low
items.raw:
Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The government will save more than it spends, says Jim Chalmers, but it won’t be a “slash and burn” budget update.
Unlike the federal budget, where we get plenty of notice of when it will be handed down, the government only gives us a few days notice for the mid-financial year economic and fiscal outlook (or Myefo).
There’s still a fair bit of work to do to finalise it all, but we’ve made enough progress to be confident that at this stage there will be a modest net save in the budget.
We’re not going to slash and burn in the budget where that would impact the payments that people receive or where it would impact some of the more sensitive parts of the economy. But we haven’t focused the savings on just one portfolio. There will be a number of savings in the mid-year update. They will be substantial, as I said. These are serious times.
You can see in the quite extraordinary reaction on the stock market just how volatile global markets are right now. I think it’s a bit of a symbol of the quite extraordinary volatility, unpredictability that we’re seeing play out in markets in the AI sector, but more broadly as well.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back. What happens next?
items.raw:
After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation. However, after The New York Times reported there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him, a board meeting that night ended with Huang’s resignation, and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was installed as the new interim CEO.
And then… Huang was back. 
In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies. Saying it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” Nvidia’s board announced his return as CEO on November 23rd, less than two weeks after his resignation.

items.title: The Apple Watch Series 12 is cheaper than ever ahead of Black Friday
items.raw:
The Apple Watch Series 12 is on sale in multiple configurations. | Photo: Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge	

If you’re still sporting an Apple Watch that launched five or so years ago, now is a good time to upgrade. Apple’s latest smartwatch, the 42mm Apple Watch Series 12 with Wi-Fi and GPS connectivity, has dropped to a new all-time low of $299 ($100 off) at Amazon and Walmart, beating its most sale price by $30. If you prefer a larger size, the 46mm model is on sale for $349 ($100 off) at Amazon and Walmart, beating its previous low by $30.
Apple Watch Series 12

Where to Buy:

 $399 $299 at Amazon (GPS, 42mm)
 $399 $299 at Walmart (GPS, 42mm)
 $449 $349 at Amazon (GPS, 46mm)

The Series 12 stands out compared to previous models with its new AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, which are made possible by Apple’s new S11 chip. For example, the watch can alert you when it detects sounds like a doorbell, alarm, or even a baby’s cry, while other upcoming features like Live Rewind and Siri Recap lets you look back at a transcript of the previous 15 seconds of conversation and get a high-level overview of the conversations you had that day. The new chip also makes Siri more responsive, so you can get answers to questions with less waiting around.
It’s not all about AI, though. The Series 12 also features redesigned health sensors that can now track your heart rate every five seconds even when you’re not exercising, which is particularly help if you have a chronic condition and need to keep a closer eye on your heart rate. It also introduces a new readiness score to help you decide how prepared your body is for the day. Other highlights include easier navigation with simple pinch gestures, and faster charging, which helps to make up for the fact that battery life is rated at up to 24 hours on a single charge, just like the previous-generation model. In our testing, the watch went from 20 to 64 percent charge in just 20 minutes, making it relatively easy to top up while showering or getting ready for the day.
Read our Apple Watch Series 12 review.
Update, November 23rd: Updated to reflect current deal pricing, which is $30 lower than when we last published this article.

items.title: HBO Max is offering one of the best Black Friday deals we’ve seen this year
items.raw:
If you’ve been meaning to catch up on Lanterns or the latest season of The Gilded Age, Thanksgiving weekend is the perfect time to do so. And thanks to HBO Max’s new Black Friday deal, new and returning subscribers can now watch both shows for less. The streaming service is currently offering a 50 percent discount for Black Friday, bringing the price of its Basic With Ads plan down to $5.49 per month (about $6 off) for one year. The promotion runs through November 30th, and you can subscribe either via HBO Max or Amazon.
HBO Max

Where to Buy:

 $10.49 $5.49 at Amazon (monthly, with ads)
 $10.99 $5.49 at HBO Max (monthly, with ads)

HBO Max has plenty of great movies and shows to keep you entertained well into the new year, no matter which plan you choose. You’ll find a wide selection of TV shows, including Heated Rivalry, Dune: Prophecy, The White Lotus, Euphoria, and Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, alongside longtime favorites like Game of Thrones and The Big Bang Theory. There’s more on the way, too, including HBO’s highly anticipated Harry Potter series, which premieres on Christmas.
There’s plenty to watch beyond TV, too. HBO Max’s extensive movie catalog currently includes films like Sinners, One Battle After Another, Marty Supreme, Backrooms, and Wuthering Heights. And if you’re a sports fan, both the Standard and Premium plans also include access to select live events from MLB, U.S. Soccer, the NCAA, and more.
What you get ultimately depends on the subscription tier you choose. HBO Max’s Basic with Ads plan lets you stream on two devices at once but doesn’t include live sports. The ad-free Standard plan ($18.49 a month), meanwhile, adds live sports and up to 30 offline downloads. The Premium plan ($22.99 a month) adds a few more perks, including 4K streaming and Dolby Atmos with select titles, up to 100 downloads, and the ability to stream movies and shows on four devices simultaneously. That said, HBO currently isn’t offering discounts on either the Standard or Premium plans… at least not yet.

“It helps Ukraine to defend itself today, but it also strengthens Ukraine’s hands in any future negotiations with Russia. … But support needs to be concrete. We have to show Putin that his attempts to weaken our support will fail.”
“Our citizens need to know that the lights will stay on, that their homes will stay warm, that hospitals, transport and communications will keep working.”
“One day it can be in the form of an arson attack against a factory or drones disrupt disrupting an airport. The next, it is sabotaged railways or cargo vessels targeted at sea and cyber-attacks.”
“It’s all happening now, and it won’t go away anytime soon. … The conclusion of all of this is that we are all targeted, that we are all affected – when it comes to our pipelines, our cables, our energy grids and our economies – and they are all interconnected. … That means that we are all in this for the long term, and therefore we must step up to the plate, to ensure that, we stay ahead of danger.”
“But if we are serious about keeping our alliance strong and secure, then all allies must pull their weight not only in 2035, but starting now. At least, everybody needs to have the credible path to get there.”
“These investments are also a boon to prosperity. There are dividends to be gained from investing more in defence. This is about real jobs for real people.”

items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.raw:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded
Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.
Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.
